Cosmicflows-4 supplies distance-modulus and redshift information for individual galaxies and groups \cite{Tully2023}. Pantheon+ supplies supernova magnitudes and a released total covariance \cite{Brout2022}. Gaia and Quaia supply astrometric fields, source identities, reported redshifts, and selection-related information \cite{GaiaCRF3,Quaia2024}. Planck supplies temperature and polarization maps, split products, and component-separation operators \cite{Planck2018IV,Planck2018VII}. Repeated windows, frequency channels, or processing choices within one experiment are correlated views of the same sources or sky.

The shear is spatial and symmetric trace-free, while vorticity is spatial and antisymmetric. Its axial vector is $\omega^a=\epsilon^{abc}\omega_{bc}/2$. Every physical contraction must refer to the same congruence, frame, epoch, and normalization.

For the four method families, $\sum_m Z_m=d_i$, the monopole column. Consequently the joint mean design has rank 12 rather than 13, and profiling the method columns leaves eight angular directions. This is a first-order fixed-distance and fixed-weight statement. Absolute calibration or a fuller nonlinear source model can change the problem. numeral_containing_text_blocks.text: The four-window group fit supplies a separate coupled finite measure: 2048 deterministic Sobol points of one 36-coordinate working distribution, with equal weights $1/2048$. The source IDs and all cross-window covariance are retained. It supports conditional functional exceedance and sensitivity calculations, without becoming a physical posterior. For one retained event, the empirical probability $0.60302734375$ has the density-ratio envelope\begin{equation}[0.301513671875,\;0.801513671875]\qquad(\Gamma=2).\end{equation} A declared floor change from $0.005$ to $0.05$ changes one depth-ratio median from $1.718693$ to $1.025396$. numeral_containing_text_blocks.text: A different exploratory comparison uses the 274-row cohort and five whole-group folds. Each numerator is a mixture of eight normalized conditional predictive densities, and each denominator is the largest conditional null density among four covariance scenarios. The arithmetic average of the five ratios is $0.000183218358755319$, with logarithm $-8.604831899198585$. Its small value means that the chosen alternative mixture did not outperform this composite null on those blocks. It is not evidence that the null is physically true.

numeral_containing_text_blocks.text: For a fixed training-measurable normalized numerator and a denominator that dominates the true conditional null density, this ratio has conditional expectation at most one \cite{Wasserman2020}. Training-parameter uncertainty need not be integrated for that elementary validity argument. The present calculation nevertheless lacks a qualified selected-source law, prospective control of adaptive choices, and an outward numerical certificate for its null-density supremum. Its arithmetic is informative as a conditional comparison; it is not reported as calibrated observational evidence.

numeral_containing_text_blocks.text: A release-level reconstruction examines whether rounded individual fundamental-plane moduli and errors can be compatible with the published group products under a proposed pooling rule and common offset. The structurally qualified subset contains $22\,599$ groups. Under the one-last-printed-place outer rounding convention, the marginal common-offset intersection is approximately $[0.0220801,0.0257960]\,\mathrm{mag}$, and no qualified group has a disjoint marginal error interval. These are necessary marginal compatibility conditions. They do not establish simultaneous modulus--error feasibility, the actual accepted subsource membership, or the quoted error law.

numeral_containing_text_blocks.text: There are 54 structural exclusions. In 46, the published count is blank while the numerical group modulus and its error are present. A blank count is not zero and is not evidence that the method is absent. The remaining eight have count disagreement. One decisive example is group 1490017: the retained individual table has one distinct fundamental-plane galaxy, while the group count is two. No deletion-only subset of a one-element set can reproduce a count of two. This excludes that particular repair model regardless of rounding or zero-point offset. It does not prove that every possible production stage is inconsistent.

The first uses one retained light curve, SN010010, with 59 released measurements and a fixed 23-row $gri$ selection. A measurement-only fit has $\chi^2/19=3.2323283$. Adding the public light-curve model covariance gives $\chi^2/19=0.8984302$, using iterated fixed-covariance least squares. This is a fixed-point procedure, not a normalized maximum-likelihood fit with parameter-dependent covariance.

A derived method for future frequency comparisons tests whether one coefficient vector explains delivered $E$ and $B$ targets simultaneously. Let $A_E,A_B,y_E,y_B$ have certified operator/vector error bounds $\epsilon_{AE},\epsilon_{AB},\epsilon_{yE},\epsilon_{yB}$ relative to exact counterparts. Suppose $s\leq\sigma_{\min}(A_E)$, $s>\epsilon_{AE}$, $R_E\geq\|y_E-A_E\tilde c\|$, and $U_B\geq\|A_B\|$. If one exact $c_*$ fits both fields, then
\begin{align}
 C&=\frac{\|y_E\|_{\rm upper}+\epsilon_{yE}}{s-\epsilon_{AE}},\nonumber\\
 \Delta_c&=\frac{\epsilon_{yE}+\epsilon_{AE}C+R_E}{s},\nonumber\\
 \tau_0&=\epsilon_{yB}+\epsilon_{AB}C+U_B\Delta_c
\end{align}
bound $\|c_*\|$, $\|c_*-\tilde c\|$, and $\|y_B-A_B\tilde c\|$. The proof is the triangle inequality applied successively to the $E$ solution, coefficient difference, and $B$ residual. Error independence is unnecessary. A residual exceeding $\tau_0$ plus its evaluation error excludes the exact relation; a smaller residual does not prove it. This section supplies a method, not a completed seven-frequency empirical result or a count of physical foreground components.
